reasons: Classification is correct: the carve-out in p0115 transfers ownership of Developments created solely by Corio (our party, the licensee/customer) to Commerce One whenever it provides ongoing support, with no licence back — an assignment of Customer-created IP to the Vendor, which fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back) and sits in walk-away territory, so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted rather than over-flagging.

Redline is substantively minimal and correctly targeted: the only change across p0115/p0116 is deletion of the trailing carve-out ('unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One ... intellectual property rights in the Developments.'), leaving 'shall be owned by Corio.' and preserving Commerce One's pre-existing ownership, the assignment sentence, the NDA/invention covenants and the future-negotiation sentence. The failed 'minimal edit' checks are artifacts of the deletion spanning the paragraph boundary / full-text replacement, not evidence of an over-broad rewrite.
Direction of the edit is right for our side (ownership retained by us, no Customer IP assigned to Vendor) and no assignment-to-Vendor language remains, consistent with the deterministic check.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what was deleted and why, and offers a sensible fallback (a support-purposes licence to Commerce One) without lecturing.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position (no express Customer Data ownership sentence; enhancements to the Software left to future negotiation) are appropriately noted in the rationale rather than redlined, which matches the playbook's treatment of minor gaps; severity 'critical' as claimed is appropriate given the IP-assignment issue.
